description: For every attempt a committed array under results/ summarizes: the full record's path relative to its run's out directory, ~/.local/state/foe/cross-harness/<run>, and the record's sha256. The archive holds these records and every other file under the eight run directories that rescore.py, gates/isolation.py, and conditions.py read, so the rescored, conditions, and isolation files and tables.md can be recomputed from it on any host.

archive.location: the asset cross-harness-evidence-2026-09-13.tar.zst of the release of this repository tagged cross-harness-evidence-2026-09-13
archive.format: a GNU tar archive compressed with zstd. Each member path is relative to the runner's state root, ~/.local/state/foe/cross-harness, so the directory it is extracted into takes the place of that root.
archive.built_with: tar --sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mode=u+rw,go+r,go-w --format=gnu --no-recursion -C ~/.local/state/foe/cross-harness -T <the paths under files>, piped to zstd -19 -T0; GNU tar 1.35, zstd 1.5.7

contents.read_by: gates/isolation.py, for the canary sentences and the evidence of the foe canary's planting
rescore.py, for the attempt root; gates/isolation.py and conditions.py, for every attempt

contents.files: <run>/attempts/<task>/<arm>/<attempt>/log/<episode>/**/episode.jsonl of every foe attempt, child episodes included
<run>/attempts/<task>/<arm>/<attempt>/artifacts/config.json of every foe attempt, the document the attempt ran
contents.read_by: conditions.py, for an arm whose condition depends on the document

contents.files: the session files under artifacts/codex-home/sessions/, artifacts/events.jsonl, and artifacts/codex-home/config.toml of every Codex attempt
contents.read_by: gates/isolation.py, for the recorded requests and the Codex canary

contents.files: root/task.json and root/grader/workspace.patch of every attempt
contents.read_by: rescore.py, which rebuilds the fixture from them and the base commit the task names

contents.files: every file under root/workspace/<path> for each path the task preserves on a stop
contents.read_by: rescore.py, which compares those files with the fixture

archive.base_commits: rescore.py rebuilds each fixture with git archive of the base commit a task's metadata.source names, from the repository that holds rescore.py. Every base commit it needs for these runs is an ancestor of main. The teams tasks name a base commit that main lacks, and preserve no path, so rescore.py builds no fixture for them.

excluded.what: every file of an attempt workspace outside the preserved paths, including target/ build outputs, the check suite's .check-tmp directories, and caches
excluded.why: none of the three scripts reads them. rescore.py hashes only the preserved paths, and build outputs are regenerated by any build. The eight run directories hold about 115 GB, almost all of it these workspaces.

excluded.what: every file under root/grader/ other than workspace.patch, such as the grade, protected.json, original.json, specification.json, units.json, the oracle workspace, and the hidden tests, and the check file beside each foe attempt root
excluded.why: the task construction and the grader wrote them. The committed arrays carry the grade, and none of the three scripts reads these files.

excluded.what: every file of a foe log directory other than episode.jsonl: the config.json and child-launch.json beside each child episode log, and the spill/ directories that hold long tool results and renderings
excluded.why: gates/isolation.py reads only episode.jsonl files, and the request events it searches are in them.
the arm record already summarizes them, and none of the three scripts reads them.

excluded.what: every file of a Codex attempt's codex-home other than its session files and config.toml: the sqlite databases, lock files, shell snapshots, temporary files, the installation id, the model and plugin caches, and the skills and plugins Codex installs
excluded.why: gates/isolation.py reads only the session files the record lists and the canary file. The installed skills and plugins are Codex's own content and are the same in every attempt.

it is a credential. The runner removes each attempt's copy when the attempt ends, and the records state credential_removed true. One copy remains on the host, in autonomy/attempts/ceiling-bound-feature/codex-default/01-interrupted-01, a directory no record names. It is excluded with that directory.

excluded.what: attempt directories no record names, such as autonomy/attempts/ceiling-bound-feature/codex-default/01-interrupted-01
excluded.why: they hold an interrupted attempt the run replaced. No committed array, record, or script refers to them.
it holds the output of gates/isolation.py, which the gate rewrites when it is run against the archive. The committed isolation files under results/ are the values to compare with.

discarded/ holds six records of attempts that ran again under the foe build every committed record of their arm used, and attempt-ledger.json lists them. The reports are report.py output for the run document. None of the three scripts reads them.

excluded.what: every other run directory under the state root, such as the development, holdout, rerun-after-fixes, shakeout, and admission runs
excluded.why: no committed table rests on them. attempt-ledger.json lists the ones the results documents mention as not archived.

credential_scan.method: every archived file was searched for credential file names (auth.json, credential, .netrc, .pem, id_rsa, token) and for the content patterns of provider API keys beginning sk- at a token boundary, GitHub tokens, AWS access key ids, Slack tokens, bearer tokens, JSON web tokens, private-key blocks, and JSON keys named access_token, refresh_token, id_token, api_key, authorization, or x-api-key with a value
credential_scan.result: no credential. No archived file has a credential's name, and no key, token, or authorization value matched at a token boundary. The sk- and GitHub-prefix matches lie inside longer strings: the opaque signature and encrypted_content fields of model responses, and build-directory names in records. The private-key blocks are the test key of crates/transport/src/auth/google.rs, which the repository already publishes, quoted in one Codex session and its event stream. The Slack-shaped strings are placeholder values of a test fixture quoted in one foe log. Records name the path of the removed credential copy, and no record holds its content.

reproduce.from: the repository root at the commit that carries this manifest, with EVIDENCE set to an empty directory for the extracted archive and OUT to a directory for the recomputed files. The isolation gate writes gates/isolation.json under each extracted run directory. Each cmp prints nothing and exits 0 when the recomputed file matches the committed one byte for byte, and git diff exits 0 when tables.md is unchanged. The isolation gate exits 4 for every run, as the results documents state, so its command accepts that status and no other. The commands can run in order under sh -e.
